title: Can Your Next Human Hire Beat an AI Agent?
summary: If meeting planners start managing AI agents, the case for adding headcount is about to get harder to make.

title: Key Corporate Event Statistics: What the Data Shows
summary: Optimism is up, but budgets aren’t. With nearly half of corporate meeting budgets flat and attendee costs still rising into 2027, planners are being asked to do the same events with less.

title: Skift Meetings Forum 2026: The Planner’s Role in a Shifting Landscape
summary: Today’s meeting planners have a remit moving further upstream into judgment, risk management, and big-picture strategic business decisions. They’ve always been expected to make complicated work look easy. The conversations at Skift Meetings Forum showed how much more nuanced and complex that work has become.

title: What a Trade Show Looks Like When the Product Can’t Actually Be on the Floor
summary: Cannabis trade shows face limits few other B2B events do: no sampling, no sales, and venues that may ban consumption anywhere on the property. MJ Unpacked, now three years into its Atlantic City run, shows how organizers design around those limits.

title: SITE and IRF Join Forces to Introduce Students to an Industry Many Don’t Know Exists
summary: An incentive travel career is often something people “fall into.” Members of the industry’s two major groups are reaching out to colleges and universities to change that.

title: Cyberattack at Moscone Center Puts Event Data Security in the Spotlight
summary: Legends Global confirms Moscone Center experienced a cybersecurity incident but hasn’t said whether data was stolen. For planners, it raises a bigger question: How much sensitive event data are venues holding and for how long?

title: Why One Supplier Decided to Create a Free Resource Hub for Planners
summary: Planners rely heavily on word of mouth to find vendors they can trust. The founder of Silicon Valley Speakers is curating an online directory to offer more options.

title: How Meeting Planners Can Avoid Falling for Sophisticated Scams
summary: The traits that make planners good at their jobs – responsiveness and an ability to meet tight deadlines – are exactly what scammers are exploiting.

title: What 20 Years of Building Events Taught Me About Their Real Value
summary: People attend business events looking for ideas, relationships, customers and opportunities. After nearly 20 years of building events, I have come to believe that their highest value is more personal: changing how people feel about the work they are returning to.

title: Steal This Idea: An Empty Chair on Your Next Stage
summary: Planners keep trying to figure out how to make meetings more engaging. Handing five minutes to an attendee for an unscripted chat is a simple way show the room its views belong in the program, not just in the Q&A.
